title: We must not limit God's knowledge because we cannot grasp how he knows; it is safer to err on the side of his knowing
source_text: LXIV. Sed certe tantum de nobis praesumere non debemus, ut divinam scientiam limitare ausimus, & negare quod Deus aliquid sciat, quia quomodo sciret comprehendere non valemus. Nam divinus intellectus omnimodo infinitus plus scit proculdubio quam valeamus capere & assequi. Saltem ille minus periculose errat, qui putat Deum scire ea quae forte scibilia non sunt; quam qui negat Deum scire quae revera scit, & quae intra divinae omniscientiae objectum continentur.
pass_a_gloss: LXIV. But certainly we ought not to presume so much of ourselves, that we dare to limit the divine knowledge, & to deny that God knows something, because we are not able to comprehend how he would know it. For the divine intellect infinite in every mode knows without doubt more than we are able to grasp & attain. At least he errs less dangerously, who thinks that God knows those things which perhaps are not knowable; than he who denies that God knows the things which he truly knows, & which are contained within the object of the divine omniscience.
pass_b_english: We certainly ought not to presume so much on ourselves as to dare to set limits to God's knowledge and deny that he knows something because we cannot understand how he would know it. God's intellect, infinite in every way, doubtless knows more than we can grasp or reach.

At any rate, someone who thinks God knows things that perhaps are not knowable errs less dangerously than someone who denies that God knows what he really does know, things that fall within the object of his omniscience.

lemmas.gloss: that we dare to limit the divine knowledge
the divine intellect infinite in every mode

choices.why: God's knowledge of all truth; 'omniscience' is the plain English term.
